propositions: When an ordered pair holds two differently-related net-active links (e.g., blocks and relates_to), a peer deletion of one relation reaches guard G5 and permanently declines removal, causing the inbound link removal path to never converge because the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every subsequent pass.

The link store API exhibits write/remove asymmetry: add_dependency is relation-scoped (keyed on target_id, relation) allowing multiple relations per pair, while the existing unlink is pair-scoped (returns most-recent link for target with no relation argument), causing G5 mismatch when the pair's most-recent relation differs from the vanished one.

Outbound ADD deduplication is direction-agnostic on (vendor_type, target_key) rather than per-relation, so when a local dep's vendor type collides with a remote link of the same vendor type in the opposite direction, the outbound ADD is skipped and the inbound remove record survives to G5 uncheckable.

Relation-scoped removal keyed on (target_id, relation) symmetric with add_dependency resolves the asymmetry: _inbound_unlink_one uses relation-scoped removal so G5-reached cases converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation, preserving the safety invariant that no link the peer still carries is ever removed.

The CLI and library facade rebar.unlink gain an optional relation argument (rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]); with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged, maintaining backward compatibility.
